main_body: Choir stall: a tall wooden panelled back with five arched niches, topped by a cornice, with a seat bench in front (red cushions on a seat board).
top_band: none: the cornice at rows 8-12 is a vertical fascia (brown with gold studs) and the seat board at rows 37-40 is a 1-3px strip; neither is a horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The whole drawing is a straight front elevation. The panelled back with arched niches is a vertical face. The seat is a thin strip of rows 37-40 with red cushions drawn face-on, so the seat has no visible depth from above. The cornice is a front fascia with no top surface. The column scan at x=24 goes from cornice tones through a dark panel (rows 16-36) to a 1-row red cushion edge and thin bench strips, with no multi-row light top band. The seat surface cannot be read from above, so the piece fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The dark outlines are tinted brown (0% neutral), which is right. The main ramps are shallow: the dark panel recesses are large areas of one brown (L=42-50) with no grain, and the wood has no plank texture or per-element highlights. The piece reads flatter and thinner than the stall and well.
